note: Clean pass with caveats. (1) The 10 items are picture stimuli: the study used one single-item novelty statement per vase image, so item_text is identical across all 10 rows and the referent lives in the item code (Novel_k = ceramic vase stimulus k, Fig 1). Per the 2026-09-05 picture-stimulus ruling the table still ships. (2) Administration language: the paper states participants were native Chinese speakers evaluated face-to-face at Lyuliang University, China, but never states the questionnaire language and publishes only English wording; S1 File (the xlsx IRW processed) has English column headers and no item text, S2 File is the lighting-item data, and S1 Checklist is an inclusivity checklist. Shipped as the translated_substitute fallback: language=Chinese, English in the base fields, _translated columns empty. (3) instructions left blank -- the paper describes the procedure but does not reproduce verbatim instructions. (4) option_text labelled at 1 and 7 only ('Strongly Disagree' / 'Strongly Agree'); 2-6 left blank, not padded. (5) Rights: no restriction located on the single-sentence novelty measure (Blijlevens et al. 2017 APiD paper supplies it; the APiD multi-item scale itself is not shipped here), and it is reproduced in a CC BY 4.0 PLOS ONE article.

PASS WITH CAVEATS. (1) The 'items' are STIMULI, not distinct questions: all ten codes carry the SAME single statement, 'This is a typical vase.' (paper, Procedures: "Typicality: 'This is a typical vase/lighting.'"), and differ only in which of ten ceramic vase images was shown. Fig 1 presents those ten vases as photographs numbered 1-10 with NO textual description, so the thing that distinguishes the items is not reproducible as text; no descriptions were invented. (2) instructions left blank: the paper describes the procedure ("Each stimulus image was accompanied by a set of independent statements, which participants rated using a 7-point Likert scale ranging from 'Strongly Disagree' to 'Strongly Agree.'") but never prints the literal instructions respondents read. (3) option_text is given only for resp 1 ('Strongly Disagree') and resp 7 ('Strongly Agree'); 2-6 are unlabelled in the source and were left blank, not padded with their own numbers. (4) Administered language: the paper never states it. Participants were 200 native Chinese speakers surveyed face-to-face at Lyuliang University, Shanxi, so a Chinese administration is all but certain, but the Chinese wording is nowhere in the record -- the S1 File XLSX (the only data deposit; headers ID/Gender/Age/Study/Typical_1-10/Novel_1-10/Liking_1-10, sheet '最新') contains no Chinese item wording, and S1 Checklist is an inclusivity checklist. Shipped under the fallback: English in the base fields, language=Chinese, _translated empty, text_source=translated_substitute, translation_source=study_supplied (the paper's own English). (5) Rights: the three single-item measures are adopted from Blijlevens et al. (2017), the Aesthetic Pleasure in Design (APiD) paper, Psychol Aesthet Creat Arts 11(1):86-98. No reserve-a-right clause -- fee, permission-required, non-commercial, no-derivatives or no-redistribution -- could be located for APiD: it has no distribution page stating terms, only an APA journal copyright notice on the article, which under the PANAS precedent is a notice about the article and not a term governing the instrument. Silence is permission, so it ships. The wording actually shipped was taken from the CC BY 4.0 PLOS ONE article. No register row was written (a round may write a block row, never a ship row). (6) Verification margin: the tightest pair is vase6 3.12 vs vase7 3.13 in Fig 2 -- a 0.01 published gap. It is still separated, because every observed mean rounds to its published 2 d.p. value (max deviation 0.005, the exact rounding bound) while a 6<->7 transposition misses by 0.010. (7) One minor residual: the paper's prose gives vase 2 as M = 4.23, SD = 1.33 while the live SD is 1.3249 (rounds to 1.32); the mean matches exactly and the SD differs only in the last printed digit.

CLEAN PASS WITH CAVEATS. (1) LANGUAGE FALLBACK: the study administered the MDI to Austrian physicians in German (the deposited .sav's only variable labels are German: 'Emotionale Erschoepfung', 'innere Leere', ...). The administered German wording is in NEITHER the S1 Dataset .sav NOR any of the paper's three supplementary tables (S1-S3 are .docx statistics tables, checked), and recoverability is scoped to those two sources, so the documented fallback was taken: canonical English in the base fields, language=German, _translated columns omitted, text_source=translated_substitute. (2) THE .sav HAS NO ITEM TEXT FOR THIS BLOCK: 21 of its 103 columns carry variable labels and none of them is an mdi column; the only mdi value labels are on MDI_perzeptile (percentile bins). So this is not a data_labels table despite the item codes being the source column names. (3) ITEMS 8 AND 10 ARE COMPOSITES: the MDI has 12 questions scored as 10 symptoms, where item 8 is the higher of 'very restless' / 'subdued or slowed down' and item 10 the higher of 'reduced appetite' / 'increased appetite'. Both alternatives are shipped in one item_text, separated by ' / '; the source prints them as '?/ ' with no space, and that spacing was normalised. (4) instructions IS BLANK: neither the paper nor the deposit prints the form's instruction line, and none was invented. The recall window is the last two weeks. (5) RIGHTS: no restriction was locatable to quote. The MDI is described by its own literature as 'available free of charge' with a downloadable manual; no fee, no-redistribution, non-commercial or permission-required clause was found on any rights-holder page, and the English wording shipped here was taken from an open-access Scand J Prim Health Care article co-authored by the MDI's own author Per Bech. Silence is permission, so no block and no register row was written.
